full_judgment: 4. Defendant Nos. 12 and 33 jointly filed a written statement to contest the suit. They denied the allegations of the plaintiffs and specially pleaded that the plaintiffs are not the successors-in-interest of Reza Mohammad and pleaded bar of limitation, defect of party and maintainability against the plaintiffs suit. Case of the contesting defendant, inter-alia, is that the originally three brothers, namely, Bengai Mahmud, Didar Mahmud and Sheikh Illias had title to the land. In 1834, corresponding to 1244 B.S., settlement operations the said land was recorded in Chitta Dag Nos. 501 and 502 in the names of the said three brothers. Subsequently said land along with other land described in the schedule annexed to the written statement was partitioned and the said land fall in the saham of Dengai Mahmud alone. After death of Dengai Mahmud his son Reza Mahmud alias Rejak Mahmud became the owner of the land and possessed the same. Thak Survey started at the time wherein the said land was recorded exclusively in the names of Rejak Mahmud in Chak No. 33 of Thak No. 3906 of the said survey operation. While thus enjoying the said land Reja Mahmud sold more or less six kedars of vacant homestead land described in schedule annexed to the written statement to three brothers, Jan Mahmud, Ajir Mahmud and Fazir Mahmud in equal share and delivered possession to them and, ever since, they have been possessing their said purchased land for more than 12 years exercising their right of possession in different ways. Said Jan Mahmud sold 1 kedar of land described in schedule to the written statement along with some other lands to his 2nd wife, Hariza Banu, in adjustment of part of demand of her prompt dower on 20th Jaishta, 1279 B.S. and delivered possession to her. Subsequently on the death of said Ajir Mahmud and Fariz Mahmud their interest to four kedars of land developed upon their brother Jan Mahmud by inheritance. Later, on the death of Hafiza Banu, one kedar of land obtained by her by virtue of aforesaid Kabid Kabala was inherited by her husband Jan Mahmud and two sons Rajid Ali and Wahid Ali. After death of Jan Mahmud the said land developed upon his two sons Hamid and Abdul Hamid by his first wife and Rajid Ali and Wahid Ali by his second wife, Hafiza Banu. After death of Rajid Ali his share was inherited by his brother Wahid Ali and after Wahid Ali’s death his interest was inherited by his two daughters, defendant No. 39, Hawarunnessa and Mymunnesa. Mymunnesa sold her interest to her sister. Hawarunnessa by registered kabala dated 19.11.1950 corresponding to 13 Agrahayan, 1357 B.S the remaining four annas share of the 2nd schedule was owned by A. Majid who sold to defendant No. 41 Hatem. After his death his seven sons, Motaher Ali, Wasir Ali, Kasir Ali, Majir Ali, Kahir Ali, Tasmir Ali and defendant No. 39 owned the land. Said Motahir Ali and others used to pay rent of their land through father of plaintiff Nos. 1-6.
